newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea Telecom share sale oversubscribed - official.
newsitem.headline: Korea Telecom share sale oversubscribed - official.

text.p: The government's auction to sell about 360 billion won worth of Korea Telecom Corp shares to individuals and corporations had been about three times oversubscribed, a finance ministry official said on Saturday.
He said deposits by applicants received on Thursday and Friday by Kookmin Bank amounted to about 120 billion won.
This meant subscriptions were for 1.2 trillion won worth of shares as applicants had to deposit with the bank 10 percent of the amount they wanted to buy, he said.
The government offered 9.62 million shares, or 3.35 percent of the company's share capital, at the minimum bid price of 37,600 won per share.
Previous auctions for sales of Korea Telecom shares, offered only to institutional investors and corporations, had been undersubscribed, pressured by a depressed stock market.
The shares will be allocated to the highest bidders.
Final results of the auction are expected to be announced next week.
The government plans to list the company on the Korea Stock Exchange in the first half of 1997.
Korea Telecom has a monopoly on the local telephone service, and holds the lion's share of the long distance and data communications markets. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5646
